title: 05. Advanced Patterns: Concurrent.futures
summary: Covers ThreadPoolExecutor, ProcessPoolExecutor, wait() and FIRST_COMPLETED, Practical Patterns.

diagrams.title: One API, two executors
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  ex["Executor interface: submit(), map(), shutdown()"] --> tpe["ThreadPoolExecutor — I/O-bound, shares memory"]
  ex --> ppe["ProcessPoolExecutor — CPU-bound, pickles arguments"]
  tpe --> fut["Future objects"]
  ppe --> fut
  fut --> ac["as_completed() / wait() / result()"]
diagrams.explain: `concurrent.futures` hides threads and processes behind the same interface, so switching from I/O-bound to CPU-bound work is often a one-word change. Use the executor as a context manager — the `with` block calls `shutdown(wait=True)` so every job finishes before you continue.

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: Basic Usage with submit()

```python
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import time
import random

def fetch_url(url):
    """Simulate fetching a URL"""
    print(f"Fetching {url}...")
    time.sleep(random.uniform(0.5, 2))
    return f"Content from {url}"

# Method 1: Using submit()
def example_submit():
    print("=== Using submit() ===")

    urls = [f"http://example.com/page{i}" for i in range(5)]

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as executor:
        # Submit all tasks
        futures = [executor.submit(fetch_url, url) for url in urls]

        # Collect results
        for future in futures:
            result = future.result()  # Blocks until complete
            print(f"Got: {result}")

# Method 2: Using map()
def example_map():
    print("\n=== Using map() ===")

    urls = [f"http://example.com/page{i}" for i in range(5)]

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as executor:
        # map() returns results in order
        results = executor.map(fetch_url, urls)

        for result in results:
            print(f"Got: {result}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    start = time.time()
    example_submit()
    print(f"submit() time: {time.time() - start:.2f}s")

    start = time.time()
    example_map()
    print(f"map() time: {time.time() - start:.2f}s")
```

#### Example 2: Future Methods

```python
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, Future
import time

def slow_operation(value):
    time.sleep(2)
    if value < 0:
        raise ValueError("Negative value!")
    return value * 2

def on_complete(future: Future):
    """Callback when future completes"""
    if future.exception():
        print(f"[Callback] Error: {future.exception()}")
    else:
        print(f"[Callback] Result: {future.result()}")

def main():
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
        # Submit tasks
        future1 = executor.submit(slow_operation, 21)
        future2 = executor.submit(slow_operation, -5)

        # Add callbacks
        future1.add_done_callback(on_complete)
        future2.add_done_callback(on_complete)

        # Check status
        print(f"future1.done(): {future1.done()}")
        print(f"future1.running(): {future1.running()}")

        # Wait with timeout
        try:
            result = future1.result(timeout=1)
            print(f"Got result quickly: {result}")
        except TimeoutError:
            print("Still waiting for result...")

        # Get result (blocks until done)
        try:
            result = future1.result()
            print(f"future1 result: {result}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"future1 error: {e}")

        # Handle exception
        try:
            result = future2.result()
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"future2 error: {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

#### Example 3: as_completed() for Fastest Results

```python
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
import time
import random

def process_item(item_id):
    """Process with random duration"""
    duration = random.uniform(0.5, 2)
    time.sleep(duration)
    return f"Item {item_id} done in {duration:.2f}s"

def main():
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
        # Submit all tasks
        futures = {
            executor.submit(process_item, i): i
            for i in range(10)
        }

        # Process results as they complete
        print("Results (in completion order):")
        for future in as_completed(futures):
            item_id = futures[future]
            try:
                result = future.result()
                print(f"  {result}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  Item {item_id} failed: {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    start = time.time()
    main()
    print(f"\nTotal time: {time.time() - start:.2f}s")
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: CPU-Bound Tasks

```python
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
import time
import math

def cpu_intensive(n):
    """CPU-intensive calculation"""
    return sum(math.sqrt(i) for i in range(n))

def main():
    numbers = [10_000_000] * 4

    # Sequential
    print("=== Sequential ===")
    start = time.time()
    sequential_results = [cpu_intensive(n) for n in numbers]
    sequential_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"Time: {sequential_time:.2f}s")

    # Parallel with ProcessPoolExecutor
    print("\n=== Parallel (ProcessPoolExecutor) ===")
    start = time.time()
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
        parallel_results = list(executor.map(cpu_intensive, numbers))
    parallel_time = time.time() - start
    print(f"Time: {parallel_time:.2f}s")

    print(f"\nSpeedup: {sequential_time/parallel_time:.2f}x")
    print(f"Results match: {sequential_results == parallel_results}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

#### Example 2: Initializer for Worker Processes

```python
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
import os

# Global variable set by initializer
_worker_config = None

def init_worker(config):
    """Initialize worker process"""
    global _worker_config
    _worker_config = config
    print(f"Worker {os.getpid()} initialized with config: {config}")

def process_task(task_id):
    """Task that uses initialized config"""
    global _worker_config
    return f"Task {task_id} processed by PID {os.getpid()} with config={_worker_config}"

def main():
    config = {'setting': 'value', 'mode': 'production'}

    with ProcessPoolExecutor(
        max_workers=2,
        initializer=init_worker,
        initargs=(config,)
    ) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(process_task, i) for i in range(6)]

        for future in futures:
            print(future.result())

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```
║  Task B: ████████████❌ ◄── Returns when B raises exception                 ║
║  Task C: ████████████████████████░░░░░░                                    ║
║                                                                             ║
║  ALL_COMPLETED (default):                                                   ║
║  ────────────────────────                                                   ║
║  Task A: ████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                                    ║

║  Task C: ████████████████████████░░░░░░ ◄── Returns when all finish        ║
║                                                                             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: wait() with Different Options

```python
from concurrent.futures import (
    ThreadPoolExecutor,
    wait,
    FIRST_COMPLETED,
    FIRST_EXCEPTION,
    ALL_COMPLETED
)
import time
import random

def task(task_id, duration, should_fail=False):
    time.sleep(duration)
    if should_fail:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Task {task_id} failed!")
    return f"Task {task_id} done"

def main():
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as executor:
        # Example 1: FIRST_COMPLETED
        print("=== FIRST_COMPLETED ===")
        futures = [
            executor.submit(task, i, random.uniform(1, 3))
            for i in range(5)
        ]

        done, not_done = wait(futures, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
        print(f"First completed: {len(done)} done, {len(not_done)} pending")
        for f in done:
            print(f"  Result: {f.result()}")

        # Wait for rest
        wait(not_done)

        # Example 2: With timeout
        print("\n=== With Timeout ===")
        futures = [
            executor.submit(task, i, 2)
            for i in range(3)
        ]

        done, not_done = wait(futures, timeout=1.0)
        print(f"After 1s: {len(done)} done, {len(not_done)} pending")

        # Wait for rest
        wait(not_done)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

diagrams.title: wait(..., return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant M as main
  participant A as mirror A
  participant B as mirror B
  participant C as mirror C
  M->>A: submit download
  M->>B: submit download
  M->>C: submit download
  B-->>M: finished first
  M->>M: wait returns done = {B}, pending = {A, C}
  M->>A: cancel() if not started
  M->>C: cancel() if not started
diagrams.explain: `wait` returns two sets so you decide what to do with the rest — the basis for "fastest mirror wins" or hedged requests. Remember that `cancel()` cannot stop a job that is already running in a pool.

sections.title: 12.5 Practical Patterns
Pitfalls & Gotchas
sections.body:
### Process Pool and Pickle

```python
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

# ❌ Lambda functions can't be pickled
with ProcessPoolExecutor() as executor:
    # This will fail!
    # executor.submit(lambda x: x * 2, 21)
    pass

# ✅ Use regular functions
def double(x):
    return x * 2

with ProcessPoolExecutor() as executor:
    result = executor.submit(double, 21).result()
```

### Shared State

```python
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

counter = 0  # Global variable

def increment():
    global counter
    counter += 1
    return counter

# ❌ Each process has its own copy!
with ProcessPoolExecutor() as executor:
    results = list(executor.map(increment, range(10)))
    print(results)  # All 1s! Each process starts at 0
```

sections.title: Performance Notes
sections.body:
| Executor    | Startup | Task Overhead | Best For  |
| ----------- | ------- | ------------- | --------- |
| ThreadPool  | ~1ms    | ~0.1ms        | I/O-bound |
| ProcessPool | ~100ms  | ~10ms         | CPU-bound |
